The paper states that after 1500 cycles, the cathode delivers a capacity of 306 mAh/gS at a rate of 1C. 

To calculate the capacity per gram of the whole electrode, we need to know the mass of the whole electrode. The paper states that the cathode delivers 87 mAh/g after 1500 cycles at 100% depth of discharge (DOD), and that this is an impressive mass specific performance especially with the moderate loading of 35 wt% active sulfur. This means that the mass of the whole electrode is 87 mAh/g / 0.35 = 248.57 mAh/g. 

The ratio of the capacity per gram of sulfur to the capacity per gram of the whole electrode is 306 mAh/gS / 248.57 mAh/g = 1.23. 

The sulfur share of the electrode implied by this ratio is 1.23 / (1.23 + 1) = 0.554 or 55.4%. 

The paper states that the cathode has a sulfur content of 35 wt%. The ratio of the sulfur share of the electrode to the sulfur content is 0.554 / 0.35 = 1.58.
